name: El Chaltén and Fitz Roy
tagline: The trekking capital of Argentina: a small mountain village at the foot of the granite spires of Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre, with free trails from the door.
highlight: Reaching Laguna de los Tres at dawn, as the first light turns the Fitz Roy needles orange above the frozen lagoon.
shortDescription: A hiker's paradise in Los Glaciares National Park, with day walks to Laguna de los Tres and Laguna Torre beneath some of the world's most dramatic granite peaks.
metaDescription: An El Chaltén travel guide: Laguna de los Tres and Fitz Roy, Cerro Torre and Laguna Torre, day hikes, multi-day treks, best time, how to get there from El Calafate, weather and a three-day plan.
nearestAirport: El Calafate (FTE), about 3 hours by road
knownFor: Fitz Roy, Cerro Torre, day hikes, climbing, Patagonian wind

image.alt: The granite spires of Mount Fitz Roy rising above forests and a valley in Patagonia

intro: El Chaltén was founded in 1985, largely to establish an Argentine presence in an area disputed with Chile, and it has grown into a village of about 3,000 people with a single purpose: hiking. It sits in the Los Glaciares National Park, in a valley beneath Fitz Roy (3,405 metres), whose Tehuelche name, Chaltén, means smoking mountain, for the cloud that often clings to its summit, and its neighbour Cerro Torre. Together, these granite spires form some of the most spectacular mountain scenery in the world.

The great appeal of El Chaltén is that the trails begin at the edge of the village, and require no permits, guides or park fees. A day's walk can reach an alpine lake with the towers reflected in it, and there is a choice of routes, from easy lakeside strolls to demanding ascents. For serious climbers, the granite walls are a legendary challenge.

The weather is the wild card. Patagonia's wind, rain and sun can change within an hour, and clear days are precious. The village is small, with brewpubs, simple hotels and a relaxed atmosphere, and it is at its best between November and March, though autumn brings golden beech forests and fewer people.

whyVisit.intro: El Chaltén offers some of the finest day hiking in the world, right from the village.

points.title: Trails from the door
points.text: No permits or fees, and well-marked paths from the village.

points.title: Iconic peaks
points.text: Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre, among the most dramatic mountains in the Andes.

points.title: Day walks for all levels
points.text: From a two-hour stroll to a full-day climb to a glacial lake.

points.title: A friendly village
points.text: Craft beer, hearty food and a community of walkers.

attractionsIntro: The walks are the attractions, and a few classic routes stand out.

attractions.name: Laguna de los Tres and Fitz Roy

image.alt: The turquoise Laguna de los Tres beneath the granite face of Fitz Roy

attractions.text: The classic hike, about 20 km round trip and 8 to 10 hours, ending with a steep final climb to a lake directly beneath Fitz Roy's summit.
attractions.tip: Start early, on a clear day, and bring warm layers.

attractions.name: Laguna Torre and Cerro Torre

image.alt: Cerro Torre rising above Laguna Torre and its icebergs

attractions.text: An easier day hike of about 18 km round trip and 6 to 7 hours, to a glacial lake beneath the needle of Cerro Torre, often wrapped in cloud.

attractions.name: Mirador de los Cóndores and Las Águilas
attractions.text: A short hike of about 1 hour up from the village, to viewpoints over the town, valley and mountains.

attractions.name: Chorrillo del Salto waterfall
attractions.text: A short, easy walk of about 3 km to a waterfall in the forest, a good option for a windy day.

attractions.name: Loma del Pliegue Tumbado
attractions.text: A high-altitude route of about 20 km to a ridge with a panorama of Fitz Roy and the ice field.

attractions.name: The Huemul Circuit
attractions.text: A multi-day trek around a glacial lake, with a river crossing and stunning views.

thingsToDoIntro: Hiking is the main activity, with options for rest days.

thingsToDo.title: Hike to Laguna de los Tres
thingsToDo.text: A day's walk to the base of Fitz Roy.

thingsToDo.title: Hike to Laguna Torre
thingsToDo.text: See the icebergs and Cerro Torre.

thingsToDo.title: Go rock climbing
thingsToDo.text: Guides offer introductory climbs on local rock.

thingsToDo.title: Try horseback riding
thingsToDo.text: Trips through the valley on Patagonian horses.

thingsToDo.title: Rest at a brewpub
thingsToDo.text: Local microbreweries offer beer and food.

thingsToDo.title: Go kayaking or trekking on the Viedma Glacier
thingsToDo.text: Boat trips and ice treks reach the Viedma Glacier.

foodIntro: Food in El Chaltén is simple and hearty, geared to hikers.

foods.name: Craft beer
foods.text: Microbreweries serve fresh beer and pub food.

foods.name: Pasta and pizza
foods.text: Hearty meals after a long hike.

accommodation.intro: Accommodation ranges from hostels to lodges, and is limited in peak season, so book well ahead.

areas.name: The village centre
areas.text: Hostels and hotels on the main streets.

areas.name: Trailheads
areas.text: Lodges at the start of trails.

areas.name: Camping
areas.text: Free and paid campsites, regulated in the park.

gettingThere.intro: El Chaltén is 215 km north of El Calafate, reached by a good road.

options.text: About 3 hours, with several daily services.
About 3 hours by road, with wide views.
Via El Calafate, or via Villa O'Higgins by ferry and trail in summer.

gettingAround.intro: Everything is on foot in the village and on the trails.

options.text: Transfers to trailheads for longer routes.

bestTime.headline: November–March
bestTime.summary: Patagonia's climate is cool and windy, with snow in winter. Summer has the best hiking weather, and autumn brings beautiful colours.

seasons.text: Longest days, warmest weather and the most people.
Windy and cool, with fewer visitors.

bestTime.avoid: Winter, when the village is nearly empty and trails are snowbound.

itinerary.title: Three days in El Chaltén
itinerary.intro: Two big walks and a rest day.

days.title: Laguna Torre
days.afternoon: Return, then bus to El Calafate.

tipsIntro: The mountains are close, but the weather demands respect.
tips: Check the weather and go on the clearest day you can.
Carry layers, waterproofs, gloves and a hat, and a windproof jacket.
Bring lunch, water and snacks, since there is no food on the trails.
Register with park rangers and follow the rules for camping and fires.
Start early. The days are long in summer.
Bring cash, as ATMs are unreliable.

faq.q: How many days do you need in El Chaltén?
faq.a: Three days is ideal, for two big hikes and a rest day.
Not for the main day hikes, which are well marked. Guides are recommended for glacier treks and multi-day routes.
The main trails have no entry fee, but check the current park rules.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: November to March, with April for autumn colours.

faq.q: How hard is the Laguna de los Tres hike?
faq.a: It is a long day of about 20 km with a steep final section. It suits reasonably fit walkers.

faq.q: Can I see Fitz Roy without hiking?
faq.a: Yes, from viewpoints near the village and along the road, weather permitting.
